Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 

GUIDELINES FOR 
ESTIMATION OF ENGINE POWER FOR 
SMALL MECHANIZED FISHING BOATS 



> 
CO 

c 



1. Scope— Prescribes guidelines for assessing the duties of small mechanized fishing boats and 
estimating engine power to meet these duties. 

2. Duties 

2.1 a) To develop free running speed in smooth water as specified by the owner/operator; 

b) To compensate for added hull resistance due to the deterioration of the hull during service; 

c) To drive auxiliary machinery, in case necessary; and 

d) To tow a trawl, in case necessary. 

3. Assessment of Power 

3.1 The power required to obtain the given free running speed shall be estimated by the designer/builder 
on naval architecture principles as well as by model testing, if necessary. 

3.2 In order to allow for reserve power to take into account the duties listed under 2(b), (c), and (d), 
the contractual speed in the trial condition of a newly built vessel shall be achieved by utilizing only 85 
percent maximum continuous rating ( MCR ). 

Note — The power requirement for towi.ig/hauling a trawl net or driving auxiliary machinery is generally between 
30 to 35 percent of the power given in 3.2. 



EXPLA N ATORY NOTE 

The objective of th)s standard )$ to he)p owner/operator of the mechanized fishing boats for 
correctly assessing the power requirement for required operation of these boats.
